interactions.summary: Jiang answers that hope is arrogant because Dante continues writing as if future generations will revere him despite having no present evidence that his poem will matter.
A student asks how Jiang distinguishes this hopeful arrogance from plain ego.

Jiang says the difference is selflessness: Dante gives his remaining life to a world-changing work instead of taking courtly praise, and this makes his arrogance sacrificial rather than merely egoistic.
Another student asks whether Dante's selfless sacrifice still assumed that his labor would eventually bear fruit.
Jiang says yes, and that expectation of fruition is precisely what hope means.

claims.claim: Jiang says hope means Dante writes as though future readers in distant places and times will love him and preserve his work even though he has no evidence of that outcome.
He argues that without this arrogant hope Dante could not have survived his final years or completed the Divine Comedy with total focus.
Jiang distinguishes hope from ego by saying Dante gives himself to humanity instead of spending his final years enjoying patrons, praise, and courtly comfort.
He says the final cantos are both extremely arrogant and extremely selfless because Dante is trying to show humanity a better future.
Jiang analogizes Dante's selfless arrogance to Jesus believing only he can redeem humanity and to Moses trusting that his people will remember him even if he never enters the Promised Land.
Jiang answers that hope includes an expectation that the sacrifice will come to fruition.

signature_moments.moment: Hope is pictured as Dante writing in exile while imagining future readers in Beijing who will worship and love him.
signature_moments.source_phrase: people in China, in Beijing, who will read me
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's vivid way of making hope into an audacious wager on posterity rather than a vague feeling.

signature_moments.moment: Arrogance becomes legitimate when it gives itself away to humanity instead of cashing out in pleasure, prestige, and patronage.
signature_moments.source_phrase: he's gifting himself to the world
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is Jiang's cleanest distinction between vanity and redemptive ambition.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's idea that real hope expects one's apparently impossible labor to bear fruit in history.

chronology_notes.note: This packet deepens Jiang's late-Dante framing by moving from despair into the internal motive that allegedly carried Dante through the final year or two of composition.
